title: Honey Soy Chicken Stir-Fry

extendedIngredients.name: chicken thigh fillets
extendedIngredients.original: 500 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

extendedIngredients.name: brown onion
extendedIngredients.original: 1 brown onion, cut into thin wedges

extendedIngredients.name: carrot
extendedIngredients.original: 1 carrot, thinly sliced on the diagonal

extendedIngredients.name: red capsicum
extendedIngredients.original: 1 red capsicum, seeded and cut into strips

extendedIngredients.name: buk choy
extendedIngredients.original: 1 bunch buk choy, stems sliced, leaves kept whole

extendedIngredients.name: jasmine rice
extendedIngredients.original: 1.5 cups (300 g) jasmine rice, to serve

steps: Cook the jasmine rice according to packet directions, then keep it warm while you stir-fry.
Stir the honey, soy sauce, garlic and fresh ginger together in a small bowl. In a cup, mix the cornflour with 2 tablespoons of cold water to make a smooth slurry.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken thigh fillets in two batches so the pan stays hot, 3-4 minutes per batch, until browned and just cooked. Set aside on a plate.
Add a little more oil to the pan, then stir-fry the brown onion, carrot, red capsicum and buk choy stems for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return the chicken and any resting juices to the pan, pour in the honey soy sauce and toss everything to coat.
Give the cornflour slurry a quick stir, add it to the pan and boil for 1-2 minutes, tossing, until the sauce thickens and glazes the chicken and vegetables.
Take the pan off the heat and toss through the buk choy leaves and roasted cashews until the leaves just wilt. Season with a good grind of pepper.
Serve the stir-fry over the steamed jasmine rice, topped with the spring onions.
